occurrence_pattern.note: Patient-reported recurring background/rhythmic sensation historically called “evening PEM”; later described as evening pulsing or tingling. May start in the morning or afternoon despite its name. The patient describes it as near-daily; absence of an entry does not indicate absence of the sensation. A severe PEM crash or poisoned state may overlap but is not a prerequisite. The patient reports a similar return or intensification during the January 2026 S-acetyl-L-glutathione (SAG) trial; the SAG-like presentation could include stronger sinus/retro-orbital/forehead pressure, though sinus pressure started before SAG. An analogous presentation was described in April 2026 after a different treatment. Similarity does not establish a common mechanism or treatment causation.

items.source_detail: Physical, cognitive and sensory activity can precipitate tingling in the forearms/legs, nape pressure, cognitive slowing, marked malaise and involuntary sleep. The patient distinguishes this from ordinary muscle fatigue. Evening attacks and repeated waves over days are described. Meals often relieved milder episodes rapidly, with exceptions.

resolution.rationale: The post-NADH pattern was still present at the practitioner review.

occurrence_pattern.triggers: Patient-reported physical, cognitive and sensory exertion; some episodes follow sleep loss, emotional effort, or treatment changes. Other episodes have no established trigger.
occurrence_pattern.note: Patient-described spectrum, not a proven single mechanism. Crashy = vulnerable/warning phase, potentially aborted. Poisoned and malaise = experiential qualities. A crash is a distinct severe endpoint, not obligatory. Deep internal tingling/pulsing and sensory intolerance remain independently recorded baseline features that often intensify with episodes. Individual observations do not establish causation or an exertional trigger.
